summary: Toshiro Yamano was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Otani University, where he also served as an assistant professor (助教授).

Specializing in Indology and philosophy, Toshiya Unebe studied under Musashi Tachikawa. Around 2003, he served as an Associate Professor in the Department of Indian Studies within the Graduate School of Letters at Nagoya University.
Totsudo Kato (1870–1949) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied under Seiran Ouchi and Enryo Inoue (circa 1887–1890). He later held a post at Nihon University.

Tou-hui Fok (1940–2018) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at New Asia College, New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies, CUHK, and Otani University. He later served as a lecturer at CUHK from around 1972 to 1986.
Tracy Franz is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. She has held posts as a teacher at Dalhousie University and as an English teacher at Shokei University.

Travis L. Smith is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley and completed his PhD at Columbia under John Stratton Hawley and Sheldon Pollock. He held posts at Barnard College and the University of Florida around 2008.

Trent Walker is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (circa 2011–2018) under doctoral supervisor Alexander von Rospatt, along with committee members Penelope Edwards, Olivier de Bernon, Robert H. Sharf, and Bonnie C. Wade.

Trevor Leggett (1914–2000) was a scholar in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied law at King's College London (circa 1931–1934) and served as Head of the Japanese Service at the BBC from circa 1946 to 1970.

Trevor Ling (1920–1995) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at the University of Leeds from circa 1963 to 1972 and at Visva-Bharati University from circa 1976 to 1978.

Trijang Rinpoche (1901–1981) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under Sherab Gyatso and the 14th Dalai Lama, whom he also taught. He taught at Ganden Shartse Monastery and instructed Herbert V. Guenther, Zong Rinpoche, and Thubten Yeshe.

Troy Organ (1912–1992) worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at the University of Iowa (until circa 1941). He held posts at Parsons College, the University of Akron, Ohio University, and Chatham University.
Trung Huynh is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of the West by 2016 under supervisor Darui Long and committee members Lewis Lancaster and Miroj Shakya.

Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche (born 1968) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who earned his PhD from Harvard University (circa 1997–2004) under committee members Leonard van der Kuijp, John J. Makransky, and Robert M. Gimello, and studied under Thomas Burke.

Tse-fu Kuan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Oxford (1999–2004) under Richard Gombrich. He conducted postdoctoral research at National Cheng Kung University (circa 2006–2008) and held a post at Yuan Ze University around 2008.

Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang (born 1951) is a Tibetology and linguistics scholar who studied at Panjab University, Tibetan Children's Village, and the University of Glasgow. He served as headmaster at Tibetan Children's Village and became Instructor in Tibetan at Oxford in 2001.
Tsering Gyaltsen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and under the traditional teacher Dudjom Rinpoche.

Tsering Shakya (born 1959) is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at SOAS University of London (circa 1981–2004), where he also held a post (circa 1999–2005), before becoming a Professor at the University of British Columbia around 2005.

Tsoknyi Rinpoche (born 1966) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under teachers Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Adeu Rinpoche. He also taught Adam Pearcey.

Tsuguhito Takeuchi (1951–2021) was a Tibetology and linguistics scholar who studied at Kyoto University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Indiana University. From circa 1999 to 2017, he served as Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies.

Tsugunari Kubo (1936–2019) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar educated at the University of Tokyo (circa 1957–1967). He served as a lecturer at Rissho University, President of Reiyūkai (circa 1975–1993), and President of the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (circa 1977–2019).
